title: RemindMe: Plugging a Reminder Manager into Email for Enhancing Workplace Responsiveness
abstract: RemindMe integrates reminder management with workplace email to reduce the cognitive overhead of handling incoming and outgoing requests. The system targets the common workplace problem of remembering follow-ups and maintaining responsiveness to colleagues.

title: HARVEST, a longitudinal patient record summarizer
abstract: HARVEST is a problem-based interactive temporal summarizer and visualization for longitudinal patient records. It aggregates information around clinically meaningful problems across time and care settings and was evaluated in point-of-care review tasks, making it relevant to persistent work-item identity and state tracking.
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association

title: CLIN-SUMM: Incremental Longitudinal Summarization of Clinical Notes Enables Scalable Representation and Early Disease Prediction
abstract: CLIN-SUMM treats summarization as an incremental longitudinal representation problem rather than repeatedly collapsing the entire history into a static summary. It constructs structured, date-partitioned representations encounter by encounter using only information available at that time, and evaluates correctness and completeness as well as downstream longitudinal prediction.

title: Communicating uncertainty about facts, numbers and science
abstract: This interdisciplinary review develops a framework for communicating epistemic uncertainty about factual and quantitative claims. It synthesizes evidence on how uncertainty communication can affect cognition, affect, trust, behavior, and decisions, and distinguishes multiple sources and forms of uncertainty.

title: Corpus-Based Problem Selection for EHR Note Summarization
abstract: As a step toward longitudinal patient-history summarization, the paper studies automatic selection of patient problems from accumulated clinical notes. Its focus on identifying problems that remain relevant to the current state provides a transferable model for retaining persistent items from long histories.

title: A case study of batch and incremental recommender systems in supermarket data under concept drifts and cold start
abstract: The study compares batch and streaming recommender systems on real data exhibiting changing user preferences and cold-start conditions. Incremental models recover more effectively under concept drift, offering transferable evidence for personalization systems that must adapt to non-stationary users.

title: TREC 2013 Temporal Summarization
abstract: The TREC track evaluates online systems that monitor developing events and emit short, relevant, reliable, and timely updates while avoiding redundant information. It also explicitly considers tracking the changing values of important event attributes and evaluates gain, comprehensiveness, and latency-related properties.

title: Can You Verifi This? Studying Uncertainty and Decision-Making About Misinformation Using Visual Analytics
abstract: Controlled experiments use a visual-analytics system to study decisions when users encounter uncertain and conflicting information from multiple sources. The presence of conflicting cues systematically changes veracity judgments, providing evidence relevant to presenting disputed information rather than hiding disagreement.

title: Interactive Multi-Objective Probabilistic Preference Learning with Soft and Hard Bounds
abstract: The framework distinguishes aspirational soft bounds from non-negotiable hard bounds in interactive multi-objective preference learning. It probabilistically learns user preferences while respecting the different semantics of these two constraint classes, providing a transferable model for precedence between hard rules and softer priorities.

title: Overview of the TAC 2008 Update Summarization Task
abstract: TAC 2008 required systems to generate an initial summary and then an update summary for a later related document set under the assumption that the reader had already consumed the earlier material. Systems were assessed using automatic metrics and manual judgments of content, readability, and overall responsiveness.

title: Strategy-Specific Decision Making with Incomplete Information
abstract: The study tests decision making when the available evidence is incomplete and varies both the amount and structure of information shown to participants. Across several decision strategies, information completeness and presentation structure significantly affect decision performance, offering transferable evidence for briefing interfaces that must expose insufficiently investigated state.
venue: Proceedings of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society Annual Meeting

title: Prospective memory: when reminders fail
abstract: Four experiments tested whether reminders necessarily improve prospective memory. Reminders specifying both the triggering event and the intended action were most effective, while target-only reminders could perform no better than receiving no reminder, showing that reminder value depends on what information is resurfaced.

title: Taking Email to Task: The Design and Evaluation of a Task Management Centered Email Tool
abstract: Taskmaster redesigns an email client around task management, embedding task-centric resources and representations in the email interface. Studies using participants' live email over two weeks found benefits from organizing messages around work tasks rather than treating each message independently.

title: How important is importance for prospective memory? A review
abstract: This review examines how the perceived importance of an intention affects prospective-memory performance. It synthesizes evidence involving rewards, relative and absolute importance, social motives, cognitive load, task type, and motivation, providing a basis for reasoning about reminder value beyond recency alone.

title: From Moments to Milestones: Incremental Timeline Summarization Leveraging Large Language Models
abstract: The approach constructs event and topic timelines from a text stream using incremental event clustering, with large language models serving as pseudo-oracles for event detection. It is evaluated across four timeline-summarization benchmarks and provides a transferable mechanism for maintaining evolving event identity over incoming information.

title: A novel temporal recommender system based on multiple transitions in user preference drift and topic review evolution
abstract: The model explicitly tracks temporal user-preference drift using transitions between time periods, a forgetting-time function, and evolving review topics. Experiments on eight datasets evaluate whether modeling preference change improves recommendations relative to static alternatives.

title: Summarize What You Are Interested In: An Optimization Framework for Interactive Personalized Summarization
abstract: Introduces interactive personalized summarization in which a summary and the model of user interests can be adapted through user interaction rather than producing the same static summary for every user. The optimization framework incorporates feedback about what information a user wants represented.

title: Mining social networks for personalized email prioritization
abstract: Presents personalized email prioritization in which importance is learned separately for each user's mailbox. User-specific social-network features and semi-supervised propagation of importance labels are combined with conventional message features to predict personal importance levels.

title: Modeling personalized email prioritization: Classification-based and regression-based approaches
abstract: Studies user-specific priority modeling for incoming email so that important messages can be processed ahead of lower-priority material. It compares classification and ordinal-regression approaches to predicting personalized priority levels.

title: Measurement of Perceived Importance and Urgency of Email: An Employees’ Perspective
abstract: Develops and validates employee-centered measures distinguishing important email from email perceived as both important and urgent. The study identifies constructs useful for modeling workplace priority rather than equating priority with simple reply behavior or message frequency.

title: Supporting Collaborative Task Management in E-mail
abstract: Examines collaborative tasks conducted through email, where interactions may extend over time and users must track multiple outstanding tasks while awaiting responses. The paper discusses reminders, grouping related communications, and combining task-relevant information in support tools.

title: Summary Cloze: A New Task for Content Selection in Topic-Focused Summarization
abstract: Defines a sequential content-selection task in which the next summary sentence must be generated given a topic, reference documents, and the already written beginning of the summary. Conditioning on the partial summary explicitly exposes what information has already been accepted when deciding what to include next.

title: Summarizing Emails with Conversational Cohesion and Subjectivity
abstract: Develops email-conversation summarization methods that exploit conversational cohesion, including quotation structure, together with subjective information to select salient material from email threads.

title: Detecting and Summarizing Action Items in Multi-Party Dialogue
abstract: Detects dialogue regions where action items are proposed, discussed, and committed to, then extracts phrases describing properties of the resulting tasks. The method uses dialogue structure and semantic information to support task-oriented summaries.

title: Beyond “From” and “Received”: Exploring the Dynamics of Email Triage
abstract: Studies how people triage email and what information helps them decide which messages deserve attention. The work examines socially salient cues that can help surface important messages.

title: Decision-Focused Summarization
abstract: Studies summarization whose content is selected for usefulness to a particular downstream decision rather than generic salience alone. The framework selects representative information while accounting for non-redundancy and preservation of decision-relevant evidence.

title: The Use of MMR, Diversity-Based Reranking for Reordering Documents and Producing Summaries
abstract: Introduces Maximal Marginal Relevance, which combines query relevance with information novelty to reduce redundancy in retrieval and summarization. The method is particularly applicable to selecting non-redundant content from multiple documents.

title: AI-Powered Reminders for Collaborative Tasks: Experiences and Futures
abstract: Studies knowledge workers' experiences with Microsoft's Viva Daily Briefing Email, which uses machine learning to surface commitments and requests embedded in unstructured email as reminders. Interviews and surveys examine what users want to be reminded about, how reminders fit workflows, and how perceived value varies with work style.
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction

title: EmailSum: Abstractive Email Thread Summarization
abstract: Introduces a dataset and models for abstractive summarization of multi-message email threads. The work highlights email-specific challenges such as understanding sender intent and participant roles and evaluates both short and long thread summaries.
